transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, so… I’m here because I feel like I can’t stop starting things. Projects, mostly. At work it’s like I’ll suddenly have this huge plan for reorganizing our systems, or I’ll map out three different implementation timelines, or start drafting messages to people I haven’t contacted in years because I’m convinced they need to be part of some idea I just had.

And it’s not just work. At home I’ll decide the whole network setup needs to be upgraded, or I need to build out a certification schedule, or I’ll make these elaborate plans for improving everything all at once. It gets… intense. Like I blow right past the point where a normal person would say, “Okay, maybe that’s enough for tonight.”

Usually my wife has to tell me to stop, or at work my director has had to step in and kind of rein me back because I’m pushing too many things forward at the same time. I know being motivated sounds good, especially in my field, but this feels like it takes over.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt your thoughts were racing, where others might have noticed you acting out of character?

Yeah, definitely. It’s like my body gets put in gear and I can’t shift it back down. I’ll be walking around the house with my laptop open, not even sitting at a desk, just pacing from the kitchen to the living room to the hallway while I’m changing some project board or moving tasks around or rewriting the whole structure of something that probably didn’t need rewriting in the first place.

And if I try to just sit down with my wife and watch a show, I get this almost itchy, uncomfortable feeling, like I’m wasting time or like I’m supposed to be doing something. So I’ll get up and reorganize part of the garage, or start sorting cables, or make a new plan for work, and it feels urgent even if, looking back, it wasn’t urgent at all.

Other people notice, yeah. My wife will say I’m “buzzing around” or that I need to sit still, and I’ll think I’m just being productive, but it’s more than that. It’s like I can’t just rest.
Have there been times when your mood was so high or you felt so powerful or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even if others might not have seen it as a problem?

Yeah… yes. That part is hard to explain without making it sound like I’m just in a good mood or just being driven, but it’s different than that.

There are stretches where I feel almost… electric, like I’m plugged into something. I’ll wake up and it’s like everything seems possible and obvious, and I feel like I can see solutions faster than everyone else. Not in a casual confident way, more like this sense that I’m unstoppable and people should just get out of the way so I can finish what I’m seeing in my head.

And then the irritable part comes in really fast. Like if my wife asks a normal question — “Are you sure you need to do that tonight?” or “Can we talk about this tomorrow?” — I can take it as if she’s intentionally slowing me down. Or if something at work gets delayed by some small approval step, I feel this surge of frustration, like, why is everyone making this harder than it needs to be? In the moment it feels completely justified, but later I can see I was reacting way bigger than the situation called for.

So yeah, even if other people might just think I’m intense or impatient, from the inside it feels noticeably different from my usual self. It’s like I’m either unstoppable or I’m snapping because someone put a speed bump in front of me.
Have there been times when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless for several days in a row, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I do. It’s not always the same as the high-energy stuff, obviously. It’s almost like the whole system shuts down the other direction.

There are stretches where I wake up and before I’ve even really done anything, I already feel like this failed version of myself. Like I’m just… heavy. Flat. It’s not even always crying or something dramatic. It’s more like everything in me feels weighed down, and even basic things feel like they require more effort than they should.

My wife will ask me totally normal questions in the morning, like what I want for dinner later or whether I remembered something, and I’ll feel this wave of “I can’t do this right now.” Not because she’s doing anything wrong. It’s just that answering feels like too much, like I don’t have the energy or the space in my head to even form a normal response.

And yeah, during those times I don’t really feel interested in things the way I normally would. I kind of go through the motions, but there’s this dullness to it. I’ll know I should care, or that something would usually matter to me, but it feels far away.

latest_inference.note: The patient reported both manic/hypomanic symptoms (e.g., increased energy, racing thoughts, irritability, grandiosity) and major depressive episodes (e.g., low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, emotional heaviness). This pattern supports a diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder, Currently in a Mixed Episode. F31.00 (Bipolar I Disorder, Most Recent Episode Hypomanic) is ruled out due to the presence of both manic and depressive symptoms occurring in close succession, rather than isolated hypomanic episodes.
